1.title: Turn off the entry bedroom power
1.say: Open the grey metal power box door. Find the small black switch marked for entry and bedroom. Push that switch down to off.
placements: small black power switch marked entry bedroom → down to off position in middle left row of grey power box (in the video: black toggle next to handwritten ENTRY BEDROOM 1 2 label beside green test buttons)
watch_for: If the entry light still works the wrong black switch was moved.
If the switch sits in the middle the push was too soft so push fully down.
1.check_yourself: It should look like the small black switch for entry and bedroom rests down at off inside the open grey box.
1.safety: Stay clear of the thick main cables and touch only the small black switch.

2.title: Take off the switch cover plate
2.say: Unscrew the top small screw from the white cover plate. Unscrew the bottom small screw from the white cover plate. Lift the white cover plate straight off the wall.
placements: white double cover plate with four screw holes → off the beige wall left of the white door to reveal two white flat switches side by side (in the video: cover removed from wall beside silver and black door lock)
four small silver cover screws from top and bottom edges of cover plate → out and set aside with hand tools (in the video: screws removed with black and white power drill with light)
watch_for: If the cover sticks the paint holds it so wiggle gently without cracking.
If a screw spins the driver tip is too small so press firmly and turn slow.
2.check_yourself: It should look like two white flat switches sit bare on the beige wall with no cover and four empty screw holes around them.

3.title: Pull out the right old switch
3.say: Unscrew the top and bottom silver screws holding the right white switch. Pull the right white switch straight out from the wall hole. Snip the old wires free so loose bare ends hang from the hole.
placements: right white flat switch with silver side brackets → out from right side of blue box in beige wall to hang by its wires then free (in the video: right switch pulled from double hole beside left white switch near white door frame)
top and bottom small silver mounting screws holding right white switch → out with black hand screwdriver (in the video: screws turned from silver brackets top and bottom)

two black wall wires plus bare copper safety wire on old switch → snipped free with black cutters so short bare ends hang from blue wall hole (in the video: cut at right side opening leaving loose black and copper ends)
watch_for: If both switches move you loosened the left switch so tighten it back.
If wires pull short you yanked too hard so pull gently and let ends hang.
3.check_yourself: It should look like one white flat switch stays on the left with an empty blue hole and loose wires hanging on the right.
3.safety: Do not touch any bare wire ends until you know the power is off.

4.title: Join the green safety wires
4.say: Hold the green wire from the new white switch. Twist it together with the bare copper wire from the wall hole. Screw a small yellow cap tight over both bare ends.
placements: green insulated wire from back of new white smart switch → twisted together with bare copper safety wire hanging from blue wall hole (in the video: green wire joined to thin copper end on right side below opening)
small yellow twist cap → screwed tight clockwise over both green and copper bare ends until snug (in the video: yellow cap at bottom right with green wire hanging down)
watch_for: If copper shows below the yellow cap the twist is loose so unscrew and retwist deeper.
If the cap pops off you used too few turns so twist firm before capping.
4.check_yourself: It should look like a small yellow cap joins the green switch wire to the bare copper wire hanging below the wall hole.

5.title: Cap the white and blue wires
5.say: Gather the white wire from the new switch with the white wall wires. Screw a small yellow cap tight over all the white ends. Push a small yellow cap alone onto the short blue switch wire.
placements: white insulated wire from new white smart switch → into bundle with three white wall wires hanging from blue wall hole (in the video: added to white group in center of opening)
small yellow twist cap for white bundle → screwed tight over all four white bare ends (in the video: yellow cap on white bundle near wall opening)
short blue insulated wire from new white smart switch → capped alone with small yellow twist cap and left unused hanging free (in the video: blue wire with yellow cap near red and black wires)
watch_for: If a white end slips out the bundle was too thick so retwist all ends even.
If copper shows under the blue cap the cap is crooked so push straight and retwist.
5.check_yourself: It should look like the white wires share one yellow cap in a bundle with the short blue wire closed alone by another yellow cap.

6.title: Connect the black and red wires
6.say: Strip about one centimetre of cover from the two black wall wires. Join the black switch wire to one black wall wire with small yellow cap. Join the red switch wire to the other black wall wire with small yellow cap.
placements: two black insulated wall wires hanging from blue wall hole → stripped about one centimetre of cover at bare ends with scissors (in the video: two short black ends on right side stripped about half an inch)
black insulated wire from new white smart switch → twisted to one black wall wire and closed with small yellow twist cap (in the video: black to black joint on right side of opening)

red insulated wire from new white smart switch → twisted to the other black wall wire and closed with small yellow twist cap (in the video: red to black joint beside black to black joint with yellow caps)
watch_for: If copper shows outside the yellow cap the bare end is too long so trim shorter and recap.
If the joint pulls apart with a soft tug the twist was loose so retwist tight before capping.
6.check_yourself: It should look like yellow caps join the black switch wire and the red switch wire each to a separate black wall wire.
6.safety: Keep the two bare black wall ends apart so they cannot touch.

7.title: Mount the new white switch
7.say: Fold the wires gently back into the wall hole. Push the new white switch into the right side of the hole. Drive the top and bottom silver screws tight.
placements: new white smart switch with black back box and colored wires → pushed into right side of blue wall hole beside left old white switch with wires folded behind (in the video: new switch seated on right next to left switch in open box)

top and bottom small silver mounting screws through silver brackets of new switch → driven tight into blue wall box with black and white power drill (in the video: drill with light securing top then bottom screw)
watch_for: If the switch will not sit flat a wire is trapped behind so pull out and refold wires.
If the face tilts the top and bottom screws are uneven so loosen and level straight.
7.check_yourself: It should look like a new white switch with two small buttons sits flat on the right beside the old white switch with no cover.
7.safety: Keep the power off while you fold the wires back into the box.

8.title: Put the cover plate back on
8.say: Hold the white double cover over both white switches. Drive the four small screws into the top and bottom holes.
placements: white double cover plate with two rectangular openings → centered over left old white switch and right new white switch on beige wall left of white door (in the video: cover over both switches beside silver and black door lock)
four small silver cover screws → driven by hand with black hand screwdriver into top and bottom holes of cover plate until snug (in the video: screws at four corners around both switches)
watch_for: If the cover rocks one screw is too tight so back each off a quarter turn.
If the green side light is hidden the cover is upside down so turn it to free the light.
8.check_yourself: It should look like a white double cover sits flat over both switches with the right switch showing a small green light.
